tasks.short: Stay abreast of trends, products, research, and treatments.

steps.what: Stay abreast of the latest industry trends.
Read notes on products she might use.
Decide which of those treatments she will keep.

tasks.design: She stays abreast by reading industry trends, products, research, and treatments herself, and she decides which treatment to keep. Nothing is drafted, nothing is filed, nothing is sent, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: What is worth keeping depends on the treatment in her hands, and a digest cannot read the trade for her.
tasks.enabler_now: No new tool is needed. The reading is already in the notes she opens.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which treatment fits her clients still takes the reading itself.
tasks.human_edge: She reads and decides. A list of headlines does not choose the treatment.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the trade and still decides which treatment to keep. She does not gain a right to skip the reading or to adopt a treatment from a headline.

reach.task: Say which new treatment the salon will not offer this season.
reach.learn: Which treatment is already refused, so she does not adopt it from a trade note.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this salon: reading industry trends, products, research, and treatments is the task. A headline list would not do that reading.
Article 50(1) applies only if a chatbot takes bookings.
A works council is required from 50 staff. Below that, article 27 consent for a booking or time-clock system does not arise.

assumptions: She reads the latest industry trends, products, research, and treatments herself, at full time. No summary is drafted and no note is filed.
No message goes to a client, a supplier, or a colleague. No product is ordered. No alert is raised. No chatbot takes a booking.
No booking system and no time clock are added, so this task does not raise article 27 consent for those systems. Nothing logs her hours or her speed.
The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
unknowns: Whether the salon already expects her to file a note of what she read.
Whether product training is paid time or her own time.
research_questions: Which trade notes does she actually read each week, and does anyone expect a written record of them?

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep on this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low and high are 0. She still reads the latest industry trends, products, research, and treatments herself, and she still decides which treatment to keep. Nothing in this task is shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Refer clients with serious skin problems to medical personnel.

steps.what: Read the client name on the client card.
Judge whether this skin problem is serious.
Refer clients to medical personnel for treatment of serious skin problems.

tasks.design: She judges the skin problem in the chair and refers the client to medical personnel in the room. A configured read on the client card ({OTHER}) shows the client name, and stays empty when that field is blank. No referral is filed or sent, no diagnosis is stored, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: Whether the skin problem is serious is what she sees now, not a field on the card.
tasks.enabler_now: The client card can show the client name when reception has already stored it.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong referral, or a missed one, can harm the client. She still makes that call.
tasks.human_edge: She judges the skin and refers the client. The name does not decide that the problem is serious.
tasks.altitude: She still judges every serious skin problem and still refers the client herself. The name on the card does not give her a right to send a diagnosis to a clinic.

reach.task: Say which skin problems the salon must refer out.
reach.learn: Which problem is already on the refer-out list, so she does not treat it in the chair.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this salon: judging a serious skin problem and referring the client are the task. Opening the client name is the small screen slice.
Salonized client cards keep appointment and treatment notes for each client.

Notes on skin conditions, allergies, or reactions are health data. Processing them is prohibited unless an exception applies, and outside a healthcare treatment contract that usually means explicit consent.

assumptions: Reception stores the client name on the client card before the visit, outside this task. That capture is not counted as saved. The field is the client name only. If it is blank, the read returns nothing and she refers the person in the chair. She does not treat a blank as no client.
No skin condition, allergy, or diagnosis is read or written. She judges and refers in the room, at full time. The spoken referral is not a letter and is not a send.
Nothing is emailed to a clinic, a client, or a colleague. No referral is filed. No alert is raised. The read does not log her hours or her speed.
The 0.2 hour allowance is confirming a client name when the card is blank. It is not the referral.
unknowns: Whether the salon requires a written referral for a serious skin problem.
Whether the client card already has a skin-problem field she is expected to fill.
research_questions: Does a serious skin problem get a written referral, or only the spoken referral in the room?

incremental.description: Confirm a client name when the card is blank before she refers the person in the chair.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a visit where the client name is blank, so the read saves nothing and she still refers in the room. High is 1, only the name read. Judging the skin problem and referring the client stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give preoperative and postoperative skin care with clinicians.

steps.what: Read the patient name on the client card.
Collaborate with plastic surgeons and dermatologists on the care.
Provide patients with preoperative skin care in the chair.
Give postoperative skin care after that visit.

tasks.design: She collaborates with the plastic surgeon and the dermatologist, then provides the preoperative and postoperative skin care herself. A configured read on the client card ({OTHER}) shows the patient name, and stays empty when that field is blank. No care plan is filed or sent, no clinical note is stored, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: The care depends on the surgeon's instructions and on the skin in front of her, which a card cannot give.
tasks.enabler_now: The client card can show the patient name when reception has already stored it.
tasks.still_hard: Preoperative and postoperative skin care can harm the patient if the timing or the product is wrong.
tasks.human_edge: She agrees the care with the clinicians and gives it. The name does not choose the treatment.
tasks.altitude: She still collaborates with the clinicians and still gives the preoperative and postoperative care. The name does not give her a right to send a care plan or to store a surgical note.

reach.task: Say which postoperative visits the salon still provides.
reach.learn: Which visit stays with the clinic, so she does not give care the surgeon still owns.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this salon: collaborating with clinicians and giving preoperative and postoperative skin care are the task. The patient name is the small screen slice.
Salonized client cards keep appointment and treatment notes for each client.

Notes on skin conditions, allergies, or reactions are health data. Processing them is prohibited unless an exception applies, and outside a healthcare treatment contract that usually means explicit consent.

assumptions: Reception stores the patient name on the client card before the visit, outside this task. That capture is not counted as saved. The field is the patient name only. If it is blank, the read returns nothing and she cares for the person in the chair. She does not treat a blank as no patient.
Collaborating with plastic surgeons and dermatologists, and giving preoperative and postoperative skin care, stay at full time. The talk is live. It is not an email and not a filed plan.
No clinical note, surgical detail, or skin condition is written. Nothing is sent to the clinic, the patient, or a colleague. No alert is raised. The read does not log her hours or her speed.
The 0.2 hour allowance is confirming a patient name when the card is blank. It is not the care.
unknowns: Whether the surgeon sends a written care order before the salon visit.
Whether postoperative visits are on the salon's books or the clinic's.
research_questions: Which preoperative and postoperative visits does the salon provide, and which stay with the clinic?

incremental.description: Confirm a patient name when the card is blank before the care visit.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a visit where the patient name is blank, so the read saves nothing and she still gives the care. High is 2, only the name read. Collaborating with the clinicians and giving preoperative and postoperative skin care stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise on makeup colors and instruct application.

steps.what: Read client name and makeup preference on the client card.
Advise clients about colors and types of makeup.
Instruct them in makeup application techniques.

tasks.design: She advises the client on colors and types of makeup and instructs the application in the chair. A configured read on the client card ({OTHER}) shows the client name and a preference the client already stated, and stays empty when either field is blank. No shade is written back, nothing is sent, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right color depends on the face in front of her, not on a stored preference alone.
tasks.enabler_now: The client card can show a preference the client already stated on the intake.
tasks.still_hard: Advising a color and showing the application still depend on the client in the chair.
tasks.human_edge: She advises and instructs. The stored preference does not choose the color or give the lesson.
tasks.altitude: She still advises every client and still instructs the application. The preference does not give her a right to order a product or to store a skin note.

reach.task: Show a stage application the client will not use at home.
reach.learn: Which technique is for a performance, so daily advice does not copy it.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge, not a measured study of this salon: advising on makeup and instructing the application are the task. A stored preference is the small screen slice.
Salonized client cards keep records of client needs and preferences.

Notes on skin conditions, allergies, or reactions are health data. Processing them is prohibited unless an exception applies, and outside a healthcare treatment contract that usually means explicit consent.

assumptions: The client states a makeup preference on the intake before this appointment, and reception stores the client name and that preference on the client card. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as saved. The fields are client name and the stated preference only. If either is blank, the read returns nothing and she advises the person in the chair. She does not treat a blank as a ban on a color.
Advising colors and types of makeup, and instructing application techniques, stay at full time. The preference does not choose the color.
No shade, skin condition, or reaction is written back. Nothing is sent to the client or a colleague. No product is ordered. No alert is raised. The read does not log her hours or her speed.
The 0.2 hour allowance is confirming a stale preference before she advises. It is not the lesson.
unknowns: Whether a makeup preference is already on the intake before the appointment.
Whether she is expected to sell the makeup she advises.
research_questions: Is a makeup preference already stored on the client card before the appointment, and who may edit it?

incremental.description: Confirm a stated makeup preference when the intake field is stale.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is an appointment where the name or the preference is blank, so the read saves nothing and she still advises in the chair. High is 1, only that read. Advising colors and types of makeup, and instructing application techniques, stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still reads the trade, still refers serious skin problems, still gives preoperative and postoperative care, and still advises and instructs makeup. A client card shows a name or a preference already stored. She does not gain a right to diagnose, to send a note to a clinic, or to pick a treatment from a headline.
reach: first-line supervisor of personal service: which new treatment the salon will not offer, so a trade note does not put it on the menu
first-line supervisor of personal service: which skin problems must be referred out, and which postoperative visits stay with the clinic
makeup artist: which application technique is for a performance, so daily makeup advice does not copy it
skills_to_grow: Refuse a drafted digest that picks the treatment for her.
Refuse a stored skin diagnosis, allergy, or surgical note, and refuse a referral letter or a care-plan send.
Refuse a makeup order or a shade written back from the advice.
role.ambitious_version: The same specialist still reads, refers, treats, and instructs. The client card only shows a name and a preference that were already stored.
